correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the slice definition of \(\mathcal T^{cc}\), localizes each chosen slice to one coordinate, and bounds the off-coordinate tail by \(\eta_\delta=(1-(1-\delta)^p)^{1/p}\). Averaging \(m\) disjoint main coordinates gives exact \(p\)-power bound \(m^{1-p}\). The center is on a separate coordinate, so disjoint support yields \(\|x_0-a\|_p^p=1+\|a\|_p^p\). The remainder is controlled by the triangle inequality. The two required limits are valid precisely for \(p>1\). Nonemptiness of slices uses only the supremum property of norm-one functionals, not norm attainment. No computational or exhaustive claim is made.

value.rationale: The statement identifies a natural cardinality effect in a published quantitative Banach-space invariant. The known two-summand scale is \(2^{1/p}\), whereas averaging many coordinate-localized slices forces the universal bound downward as \((1+(n-1)^{1-p})^{1/p}\) and to at most one for an infinite family. This is a structural distinction specific to the convex-combination index, not a parameter renaming, table recomputation, or routine single-case estimate.
